1.survey: The outposts have been comparing charts. None of us has a good record of this spot yet.
1.delivery: One crew offered to take this part of the run. It would help if another ship could take the next leg.
1.rescue: A crew's stuck away from the dock. The workshop can look at the ship once someone brings it in.
1.hunt: The crew that lost this sent a note around the outposts. Maybe a fresh pair of eyes will help.

2.survey: The hauling crews keep giving me different notes about this patch. A proper chart would help the next crew through.
2.delivery: One of the crews has already pulled a long shift. Can you take this leg so they can head back to the dock?
2.rescue: A pilot called in before their ship stopped moving. There's a place for them here when you bring them in.
2.hunt: A crew came in short one item. They checked the hold twice before asking us to put this up.

3.survey: Pilots have been describing this spot by what they can see from a distance. A closer look would settle it.
3.delivery: A current rider left this with us. They gave it another look and decided it needed a steadier ride.
3.rescue: A pilot has asked for a tow. They did the right thing calling us instead of making another try on their own.
3.hunt: A rider lost something on the way in. They remembered enough about the trip to give us somewhere to start.

4.survey: An instructor wants a better chart of this spot. It's easier to teach a route when everyone has the same map.
4.delivery: One of our practice crews has a lot on today. They asked if someone else could make this run.
4.rescue: The pilot called before trying anything risky. That's what we teach here. Now they need someone to tow them in.
4.hunt: Someone lost an item on a flight and went over their route with an instructor. Here's the area they narrowed it down to.

5.survey: The couriers have notes on either side of this spot. One good look could help them join up their charts.
5.delivery: A courier took on the first leg. We're looking for someone to take this one.
5.rescue: A courier passed along a call for help. The pilot still needs a ship that can tow them in.
5.hunt: The last courier to see it left a note. It gives us a search area, even if it doesn't give us the exact spot.

6.survey: Two settlements have tried to chart this stretch from opposite sides. They're missing the same bit in the middle.
6.delivery: A neighbor is expecting a delivery. They don't have a ship free to come and get it.
6.rescue: Someone picked up a call from a ship that can't get home. The neighbors have made room for it at the dock.
6.hunt: When something goes missing here, we ask the neighbors to look too. This time we'd appreciate a ship that can get out there.
